frontier.hypothesis: Canonical-asm authorization under the GTE-leaf carve-out remains the disposition, and session 9 completes its evidentiary case: the target bytes are now measured unreachable from C under the compiler that ACTUALLY SHIPPED THE GAME, not merely under the reference port. Every non-human author of the delay-slot ctc2 has been individually eliminated by measurement.
frontier.mechanism: Four orthogonal results now stand. H1: reorg.c:730-735 stop_search_p halts fill_simple_delay_slots at any asm insn, so cc1 can never place the delay-slot ctc2 there (32/32 hand spellings, ~164k permuter iterations). H23/H24 (new): the ORIGINAL PsyQ cc1psx (GCC 2.7.2.SN.1) emits instruction-identical output to our fork on three chassis — same {$2,$3,$5,$6,$7,$8,$9,$10} allocation, same bare j $31 — and fills the same slot with a trailing plain C store, so both proofs hold for the shipped compiler and the last 'our toolchain is a lossy stand-in' objection is measured false. H20: whole-binary census of 1,369 jr $ra tails proves ASPSX 2.34 never filled delay slots either. H16: reload1.c:3606 order_regs_for_reload requires $2,$3,$5,$6,$7 to be regs_ever_live for the eight values to land on $t0..$t7, and the target's own 17 instructions mention none of those five. Precedent is in hand and citable: func_80052B44, src/text1b.c:10995, inline_asm_canonical.txt:340, authorized 2026-07-27 for the identical construct one function later in the same file, and that ruling (docs/grind/decisions.md:1805) explicitly provides for per-function sibling rulings.
frontier.next_probe: Driver/owner step, not a grind-session step: assign escalation modality or rule directly. This session's modality was rederive and no OWNER-ESCALATION entry naming func_80052B00 exists in docs/grind/decisions.md, so it returns progress rather than disposing of the function. The operator sequence is unchanged: apply memory/grind/func_80052B00/candidate.c over src/text1b.c:10969-10994, add the inline_asm_canonical.txt entry, run `retire func_80052B00` (drops regfix.txt:3411) and `verify-oracle`; a fresh layer-2 cheat-reviewer still runs on the C.

frontier.hypothesis: The disposition is a BLOCK question, not a per-function one: game_2d_CheckLifeGaugeNoDisp, func_80052A88 and func_80052B7C are the same construct as func_80052B00, in the same contiguous authoring unit, with the same single-rule signature — so whatever ruling this function gets should be written to cover the run 0x80052A80-0x80052BDC.
frontier.mechanism: F3/H21: these four plus the already-authorized func_80052B44 are the complete set of tree functions whose jr $ra delay slot holds a cop2 op, they occupy consecutive addresses, and each of the four unauthorized ones carries exactly one regfix rule — a fill_delay pulling the immediately preceding instruction (four of only six such rules tree-wide). All three siblings are active queue items that will reach the top after this one, and the 2026-07-27 ruling already anticipated them by name. Session 9's H23/H24 apply verbatim to all four: they are facts about GCC 2.7.2 (both forks) and about ASPSX, not about this function's C.
frontier.next_probe: When any sibling reaches the queue top, do NOT re-derive sessions 1-9 on it: cite evidence.md Session 8 F1-F3 and Session 9 H23/H24, plus s8/cop2_partition.txt, s8/slotcensus.txt and s9/fused8.psx.s, re-run only the cheap per-function confirmations (target tail shape, its single fill_delay rule, sandbox --disable all), and take the disposition straight to the driver. A single owner ruling covering the block would retire four queue items at once.

frontier.hypothesis: The one acknowledged loophole in H16 — a construct whose insn exists at reload entry but is deleted by a post-reload pass, setting regs_ever_live at zero emitted cost — is still open in principle and still not worth a session; session 9 additionally notes the two constructs that would trivially close it are both forbidden.
frontier.mechanism: regs_ever_live is latched before reload runs, so occupancy established by an insn that flow2 or jump2 later deletes would be free. Every construct measured in sessions 1-8 either emits the instruction (ctlE, ctlI, occ3/occ5) or fails to set occupancy at all (unused params in s6 ctlF/ctlG, varargs homing in s7 ctlJ). The two zero-cost routes that WOULD work — an __asm__ clobber list naming $2/$3/$5/$6/$7, and register T x asm("$N") pins — are register pins by another spelling, forbidden and score-inert under the cheat-invisible sandbox besides (recorded analytically at hypotheses.md:324/385/409, never measured because measuring a cheat buys nothing). Session 9 did not probe this axis.
frontier.next_probe: Unchanged and still LOW value, recorded so nobody re-derives it and nobody overclaims the proof: grep the post-reload passes in tools/gcc-2.7.2 for their deletion conditions and try to manufacture a C source that hits one. Even a hit leaves the delay slot, which H20 and now H24 show no stage of EITHER toolchain can fill from C — so the floor still could not reach 0. Do NOT spend a session on this ahead of the disposition in frontier item 1.
